title: Update examples with getInitialProps to SSG
body:
With the release of [Next.js 9.3](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-9-3) we are empowering all Next.js applications to take advantage of the [JAMStack](https://jamstack.org/), before this, around half of our examples were using `getInitialProps` for data fetching in pages, and even though we are not removing it any time soon, it's not ideal for most applications. You can read more about this [here](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching).

Around half of our examples (110+) are using `getInitialProps`. and in most of those examples it can be replaced with [getStaticProps](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching#getstaticprops-static-generation) to take advantage of [SSG](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/pages#static-generation-recommended).

Any updates to take advantage of SSG in current examples using `getInitialProps` are deeply welcome and will be merged ASAP

PRs for New examples using `getStaticProps` / ` getStaticPaths` and removal of current examples that are very outdated or not worth upgrading are also very welcome.

Here are some of the examples currently using `getInitialProps`:

~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/amp-first~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/analyze-bundles~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/api-routes~~
https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/auth0
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/blog-starter~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/custom-server-express~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/data-fetch~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/ssr-caching~~
~~https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/using-router~~

To find more examples, do a global search inside our examples for `getInitialProps`, and with the exception of `pages/_document.js` any other result is one that we don't want!

If an example can only work with `getInitialProps`, updating it to use [getServerSideProps](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching#getserversideprops-server-side-rendering) is also welcome.

**Update:** Please create a PR per example update, this will speed up the review and merge process :pray:

title: Isomorphic env config is a severe risk of secrets leak due to developer errors
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, using Next config `env` will allow user to define variables that can be consumed both server side and client side using `process.env`.

This pattern is rather safe, because `process.env.FOOBAR` is hard-replaced directly in the code. So client-side never have access to server-side env variable.


EXCEPT if you accidentally call them.

Simple example: 
- I have called my stripe keys `STRIPE_PUBLIC_SECRET` and `STRIPE_SECRET` 
- I mistakenly think that `STRIPE_SECRET` is the public key (yeah I am dumb but its 3am and I am tired)
- User opens up the client-side code and find this variable
- I am ruined

**I insist that the system in itself is sound and safe. The mistake is on the developer side here.** But still, we could prevent that to happen at the framework level.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Force a different syntax for client side environment variables, never allow to get variables that do not match this syntax. 
The current isomorphic pattern seems nice but it's counter-productive regarding end user safety, with potentially an extremely high criticity.

CRA uses a prefix for client side variables. Limitation is that it's harder to use.

Meteor uses only runtime-like settings, with a separate `public` object in the settings:
```js
public: {
    foo: "I am available client-side and server side through Meteor.settings.public"
},
bar: "I am server only" // in Next, I would be available in the client if the developper explicitely write "process.env.bar", that's where the leak can happen
```
I would prefer a symmetrical pattern though with "public"/"private"

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Since nested objects work fine, I already enforce this pattern locally in my app, by using a `public` object.

Maybe we could add a build rule (somehow?) to check that only `process.env.public` are allowed client side.

Usage
  $ next build <dir>

  <dir> represents where the compiled dist folder should go.
```

However, the [build](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/cli/next-build.ts#L45) function is called with `<dir>` as an argument and it is then used as the root dir for some calls, like [findPagesDir](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/build/index.ts#L164).

This results in an error saying the `pages` folder is not present in `<dir>`, but according to the documentation the `<dir>` folder should only be used as the destination for the compiled app.

## To Reproduce

1. Create simple next project
2. run `mkdir dist && npx run build dist`

## Expected behavior

Application should be correctly compiled into the `dist` folder.

title: New Cookie Auth Example
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The current `with-cookie-auth` example is lacking

## Describe the solution you'd like

If the following is actually secure and preferable (newer to cookies), I'd love to improve that example or build a newer, larger one for everyone.

From what I've read (#10062 and #9913), a cookie needs to be set in the Next API route (with plain old 'cookie' and `setHeader`) with the following to be secure:
```
secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
httpOnly:  true,
expires: 'Same date/time here',
sameSite: 'Strict'
```

> **Implementation details:** I'm using Next with an external Express API on a different origin. The user would be stored in a React Context Provider along with a JWT used to verify user on CRUD operations. So when a user logs in or signs up, we'll send a sessionID, user object, and that a JWT.

In my case, I want to store a sessionId (sid) in a cookie, so that if the user closes the tab and comes back within a day, they'll automatically be logged back in. So after the Context Provider mounts, we'd make a fetch request to a Next `verify` API route. If there's a `sid` cookie, we'll send that to our external API to get the user object and that JWT. Both of which would be put in our User Provider. 

We'd have to include the cookie in the fetch like this, since it's cross domain.
```javascript
fetch('external api url', {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { cookie: 'attach the cookie here' }
})
```

We're not storing the `sid` in localStorage or a client-side cookie, so that would be secure. Would sending the cookie through the header to the external API be okay? 

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Well I could do an unsecured method using a client cookie or localStorage, but I'm trying to avoid doing that since it's not secure. 

## Additional context

@lfades I saw you comment on both the issues I linked above. Maybe you could give some insight into if an example like this would be beneficial to the community.

title: Can't type a pure JS component in TypeScript when dynamically imported
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Say you want to import `react-leaflet`, which is not SSR friendly (call to `window` global), and do not include TS typings as far as I know.

You are supposed to do:
```js
const Map = dynamic(() => import("react-leaflet/lib/Map"), {
  ssr: false
});

const MyMap = () => (<Map className="hello" />) // className won't be allowed
```

It won't work, `className` prop is not recognized on `Map`.

Now, install `@types/react-leaflet` to add TypeScript. It still don't work.

Now you may want to add an explicit type to `dynamic`, like this `dynamic<MapProps>`. But you have no way to either load `MapProps` type globally nor to import it from  `@types/react-leaflet` (not allowed in TypeScript, you have to import `react-leaflet`, which you can't server side, back to square 1).

Related: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/4515

## To Reproduce

Code above in a page should be enough to repro in  Next + TS app, VS code will show an error on `className` prop.

## Expected behavior

`Map` component typings should work directly without aditionnal step, as if you imported it directly from `react-leaflet`


## System information

- Version of Next.js: 9.3

## Additional context
I already have the following quickfix:

Eventually I had too:
- Install `@types/react-leaflet` => to get the typings
- Copy paste  `node_modules/@types/react-leaflet/index.d.ts` in my code, as  `typings/react-leaflet.ts` (to bypass @types forbidden import)
- import types from there `import { MapProps } from "~/typings/react-leaflet"`
- `const Map = dynamic<MapProps>(() => import("react-leaflet/lib/Map"), { ssr: false})`
- Enjoy

Related SO question: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60829472/dynamically-import-a-typescript-type

# Bug report

## Describe the bug
Running into an issue where importing CSS files within my nextApp works perfectly fine, however, installing a library that has only been transpiled (with babel) but not compiled with a module bundler like webpack breaks the build because one of its files has a css import - the same library works perfectly with regular react + webpack setup.

Also tried extending webpack through next.config.js with no luck:

next.config.js

```
const MiniCssExtractPlugin = require('mini-css-extract-plugin')
const cssLoaders = ['css-loader']
const sassLoaders = ['css-loader', 'sass-loader']

module.exports = {
  webpack: config => {
    config.module.rules.push(
      {
          test: /\.css$/,
          loader: [
              MiniCssExtractPlugin.loader,
              ...cssLoaders
          ]
      },
      {
          test: /\.scss$/,
          loader: [
              MiniCssExtractPlugin.loader,
              ...sassLoaders
          ]
      }
    )
    config.plugins.push(
      new MiniCssExtractPlugin(),
    )
    return config
  }
}

```

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Create the most basic fresh next.js app using latest version
2. Import CSS file and observe how it works perfectly
2. Now yarn install or link a library that has been transpiled (with babel) but not compiled with a module bundler like webpack, and one of its files has a CSS import (pretty sure it can be any non JS import)
3. Try to yarn build your nextJS app and observe it crashing with error saying CSS module not found

title: Preview does not work for existing, static paths
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

When requesting a static path generated by `getStaticPaths` with **preview mode on** (by using `setPreviewData`),
- **in dev** `getStaticProps` is called but `context.preview` and `context.previewData` are undefined.
- **in production** `getStaticProps` is never called.

A common scenario for this bug to occur is when:
- Having an existing, published, and statically built article in a headless CMS
- Then editing the contents without changing the slug
- And previewing the changes

## To Reproduce

1. Setup https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/cms-datocms
2. Publish and build a blog post
3. Change the article
4. Preview changes
5. No changes will be visible

## Expected behavior

Refering to the documention, I'd expect that (...)

> If you request a page which has getStaticProps with the preview mode cookies set (via res.setPreviewData), then getStaticProps will be called at request time (instead of at build time).

(...) also for pages that are known to `getStaticPaths` and were already built.

- Version of Next.js: 9.3.1

## Workaround

Right now I am attaching a custom preview indicator when starting a preview session in `pages/api/preview.js` and redirecting to the corresponding post:

```js
res.writeHead(307, { Location: `${url}__preview__` })
```

In `pages/posts/[slug].js` due to the `__preview__` indicator this URL was not pre-built by `getStaticPaths` and triggers a `fallback` call to `getStaticProps`. Like this I use this indicator to identify preview mode

```js
const [slug, previewIndicator] = params.slug.split('__preview__')
const preview = previewIndicator === ''
```

title: Preview cookies not passed for sequenced redirects
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

When redirecting from a third party application to a next app that uses `setPreviewData` to set preview cookies to then itself redirect to a page that wants to consume preview data in `getStaticProps`, no cookie will be attached to the request and therefore `previewData` will be empty.

A common case is a headless CMS that redirects an editor to a preview endpoint in order to review changes.

## To Reproduce

Use an affected browser (Safari or Firefox) and

0. Open private window or clear cookies
1. Visit https://next-preview-mode-redirect.now.sh/api/redirect
2. You get redirected to https://next-preview-mode.now.sh/api/preview and `setPreviewData`
3. You get redirected to https://next-preview-mode.now.sh/test **with no cookie headers set**!

### Source Code:

1. Preview Mode App: https://zeit.co/pex/next-preview-mode/7dtqcyof8/source
2. Simple Redirect App: https://zeit.co/pex/next-preview-mode-redirect/o34d2dx4h/source

## Expected behavior

The final page in the redirect chain should always render `Preview mode is On` when comming from `https://next-preview-mode.now.sh/api/preview` regardless of the referrer or browser. Therefore the preview cookies always need to be passed in request headers.

Beeing redirect should just work as accessing https://next-preview-mode.now.sh/api/preview directly.

## System information

- OS: macOS, Windows
- Browsers: Firefox, Safari
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.1

## Additional context

Chrome, Edge and Internet Explorer work as expected.

*This issue was extracted from my monologue in #11298.*

body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Static assets served from the `static/` folder will 404 if they contain URL-encodable symbols.

> Note: This issue is identical to #10004, but pertains to the `static/` folder instead of the `public/` folder.

## To Reproduce

1. Create a new Next.js Application
   ```
   yarn create next-app test-static
   cd test-static
   ```
2. Create a static file with a unique name:
   ```
   mkdir static/
   echo "hello world" > static/hello%20copy.txt
   ```
3. Start the development server and issue a request for the file:
   ```
   yarn dev
   curl http://localhost:3000/static/hello%2520copy.txt
   ```
4. See a 404 instead of file contents.

## Expected behavior

Running the following:
```
curl http://localhost:3000/static/hello%2520copy.txt
```

Should respond with the file contents, not a 404.

## To Reproduce

/* note that next.js currently cannot be configured to use another file than tsconfig.json, therefore we cannot rename it */
{

# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Until next.js 9.2.1 I could return a 404 for a page when throwing an error with `code = 'ENOENT'` in `getInitialProps`. That no longer works in 9.3.2, now a 500 is returned. This is bad for SEO, we need to be able to throw 404s.

export class Custom404Error extends Error {

        super(message)
        this.code = 'ENOENT' // triggers a 404 in next.js

}

```tsx
// ./pages/home.js
export default function Home () {
  throw new Error('hello')
}
```
or
```tsx
// ./pages/home.js
export default () => {
  throw new Error('hello')
}

title: with-segment-analytics example reports incorrect data on client-side transitions
body: # Bug report ## Describe the bug Following [the example](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/examples/with-segment-analytics/components/Page.js) for client-side `analytics.page()` calls results in data from the previous page being sent. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository: 1. Install Segment in a Next.js project according to the example repo 2. Click a "next/link", resulting in a client-side route change 3. `analytics.page()` is called with `path`, `url`, etc. from the previous page ## Expected behavior `analytics.page()` should be called with the current page info ## Screenshots In this screenshot I called `analytics.page(url)` inside of `Router.on('routeChangeComplete', (url) => {...})` as per the example. Path should be `/start`, but instead is `/`. Also worth noting the `/start` page event you see at the bottom of the screenshot was from a full page refresh, not a client-side transition. You can clearly see the difference. ## System information - OS: macOS - Browser: Chrome - Version of Next.js: 9.3.3 ## Additional context In my case I fixed the issue by overriding the default Segment properties with properties I parsed from the `url` in the callback (using new URL()). This is a little tricky and hard to generalize, since it can depend on whether or not you're using absolute or relative paths in your `asPath`s. The real solution is probably figuring out how Segment determines these values and why there is an inconsistency between those and the values in `next/router` when `routeChangeComplete` is fired.

title: Does not work with Redoc - e.trim is not a function
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Redoc library does not work with Next.js library starting from 9.1.5 (native-url was added in 9.1.5).
Next.js library in their webpack config override node-url with native-url: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/search?q=native-url&unscoped_q=native-url
Which causes an issue when Redoc library dependency (json-schema-ref-parser) trying to parse already parsed url.
## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Steps are provided on the screenshot below. 
Basically, try to parse string with native-url and then parse it again.

`const nodeurl - require('url');`
`const nativeurl = require('native-url')`
`nodeurl.parse(nodeurl('http://example.com))` <- works
`nativeUrl.parse(nativeUrl.parse('http://example.com'))` <- throws e.trim is not a function

## Expected behavior

native-url library doesn't throw an error when we try to parse already parsed string

## Screenshots

https://ibb.co/QcWHT9T

## System information

- OS: Windows
- Browser (if applies) I guess everywhere, but I checked only Chrome
- Version of Next.js: starting from 9.1.5 and till the latest one

## Additional context

Redoc has json-schema-ref-parser dependency which contain http.js file (https://github.com/APIDevTools/json-schema-ref-parser/blob/master/lib/resolvers/http.js).
Look at lines 75 and 98 to see that they parse already parsed url. This behaviour works in node-url (https://nodejs.org/api/url.html)out of the box, but next.js overwrite it with their own native-url package in their webpack config. And native-url package doesn't handle parse of parsed string.

When enabling preview mode on a SSG page, using `router.replace()` to reload the page's data only works once and is ignored thereafter.

title: Allow Babel config file name `.babelrc.json`
body:
# Feature request
On the Babel website it states you are allowed to use the `.babelrc.json` file name when creating a configuration file. With Next.js, this does not work. Only `.babelrc` is allowed. I believe it would be clearer and less error prone if Next.js would allow more Babel configuration file names.  

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When you accidentally use `.babelrc.json`, you are not notified of this. The only difference between `.babelrc.json` and `.babelrc` currently is the console message `Using external Babel configuration` which is easy to miss.

## Describe the solution you'd like

If allowing more file names is not an option, please warn the user if Next.js found a `.babelrc.json` file in the project directory so the user knows they've made a mistake. Also, please update the docs to more clearly warn the user that only exactly this file name is allowed

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Allowing just `.babelrc` is very limiting, especially because the Babel documentation talks about multiple allowed file names. This causes confusion and can cause problems (Babel plugins not working) that are hard to debug because there is no warning about using the wrong file name.

title: create-next-app always uses yarn if it is installed
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I have both `npm` and `yarn` installed in my laptop. When I create a new app using `npm init next-app` (or `npx create-next-app`), Next always uses `yarn` as the package manager. This is because it [just checks](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/packages/create-next-app/helpers/should-use-yarn.ts) if `yarns` is installed and decides to use it.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Ideally, I'd like this command to check if the command is run using `npm` or `yarn` and use the same as package manager for the new app. I'd suggest to use [is-npm](https://github.com/sindresorhus/is-npm) package (or just copy those few lines 😛, if we don't want to add a dependency) and check if code is run using `npm` or `yarn`. If for any reason this module isn't able to determine the used package manager, we can use the current logic as a fallback mechanism.

I'm happy to submit a PR is this makes sense.

title: routeChangeComplete event called on page load for routes with params
body:
## Describe the bug

When ASO is enabled and you navigate to pages with params the `routeChangeComplete` is called. On page load:

- `router.query` is `{}` on first load, but [apparently that's expected](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/router#router-object).
- `routeChangeComplete` is called.

This is a problem because `routeChangeComplete` isn't called when loading pages that don't have parameters. This inconsistency makes things difficult. 

In my case I'm trying to call analytics events on route change and page load. The page view event is called on page load (using an effect) but then the `routeChangeComplete` is immediately called which fires the page view again. 

## To Reproduce

[Reproduction example here](https://github.com/anthonyshort/next-bug-example)

Steps to reproduce:

1. Start the server
2. Go to `/` and see that `route change` is NOT logged
3. Add any query param, e.g. `/?id=1`. Reload the page and notice `route change` is called
4. Go to `/posts/1` and see that `route change` is logged on page load
5. Add getInitialProps to _app and this doesn't happen any more

## Expected behavior

I would expect either:

1. Route change is always called on page load while ASO is enabled.
2. Route change is not called on page load for pages with params

(I'd also not expect the query object to be empty, but that's probably a separate issue)

## Screenshots

N/A

## System information

- OS: macOS
- Browser (if applies) Chrome
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.4

N/A

title: getStaticPaths with fallback true: Allow custom HTTP status codes
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Using getStaticPaths with `fallback: true`, pages that are not SSG'ed yet get served with HTTP status 200 no matter what, which makes sense as the response is immediate and getStaticProps is then called in the background.

However, i need a way to:
1. server side generate static pages on demand (e.g. i have a lot of product pages and can't generate them all at build time), AND:
2. serve a proper 404 status code for product page urls that don't exist

## Describe the solution you'd like

I should be able to configure the "fallback" mode so that it's possible that the response is _not_ immediate and Next instead waits for getStaticProps to return and only _then_ sends the response, allowing me to set the HTTP status code.

For example, instead of only having one `fallback` prop, have an `onDemand` prop and a `fallback prop`.
- `onDemand`: If true enables on-demand generation of static pages. If false, all pages returned by `getStaticPaths` are generated at build time and any other pages return 404s.
- `fallback`: If true enables fallback mode as it is currently implemented. If false, for pages that are not generated yet a response is sent only after the Promise returned by getServerProps resolved, allowing tweaks to a server response (e.g. setting `statusCode`). Only has any effect if `onDemand` is true.

Of course that would not be backwards compatible so it needs some thought. But i guess something like this could work, no?

## Describe alternatives you've considered

n/a

## Additional context

#11644
author: claus

title: Dynamic routes with multiple variables per path segment
body:
# Feature request

It is currently not possible to create advanced dynamic routes which have multiple variables in a single path segment.

An example of such a route would be `unpkg.com/nextjs@v0.1.0`. This URL has variables in the first path segment: the package name and the package version. Currently the only way to handle cases like these in NextJS are to have a `pages/[identifier].js` file, and then manually split the identifier in the page component. Let's say you also have a page `unpkg.com/nextjs` which has different content to the first route. In this case you now have to deal with the extra case for `[identifier]` because you have a shared route for both, and you need and you might be shipping unnecessary code in a bundle because NextJS is not aware of the difference between these routes.

## Describe the solution you'd like

It would be great if you could just create a page like this: `pages/[package]@[version].js` and also `pages/[package].js`. Now NextJS will match these routes in the order of most specific to least specific, so `unpkg.com/nextjs@v0.1.0` would be matched by `pages/[package]@[version].js` and not `pages/[package].js`. The specificity would work similar to how specificity works for dynamic routes now. In the case of `unpkg.com/nextjs@v0.1.0` the params passed to the page would be `{"package": "nextjs", "version: "v0.1.0"}` 

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Manually doing routing in the page component, but this is bad for bundle size and also less nice for the developer. This is especially true if different multiple variables path segment paths have different subpages because then you manually have to do a lot of routing.

As an example: Use the post's example in the [documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching#simple-example-1). I have a page `/pages/stores/index.js` and `/pages/stores/[slug].js`. When I wrap `next/link` around these links I get different behavior.

and render my page properly.

but click on `/stores/foo` will fetch
1. (**404**) `_next/static/development/pages/stores/foo.js`

Create posts/post examples with `getServerSideProps` and wrap the link to the pages with `next/link`. **Use client-side routing**.

At least it should not return status code 404 but I would also expect that the page can be rendered on client-side in the same way as `/stores`

When using router.push with a relative url on older browsers, it will throw an error (in dev) or silently fail (in prod). E.g.

```jsx
function Component() {
  const router = useRouter()
  return <button onClick={() => router.push('/foo')}>Click me</button>
}
```

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Trigger a Router.push call as explained above
3. If URL is supported by the browser, all is well
4. If URL is polyfilled you'll get a `Invalid href passed to router`

## Expected behavior

There should be no discrepancies between the 2 behaviors

## System information

- OS: macOS, Windows
- Browser: tested on Chrome 49, IE11, probably others
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.4

## Additional context

I tracked the issue down to this call here

https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/b274fe39d38111588e625342a89dc568ad38fff5/packages/next/next-server/lib/router/router.ts#L395

this will evaluate differently based on whether or not the polyfill is used.
When the native URL is used, `protocol` will be `null`, when the polyfill version is used, `protocol` will be `http://`, thus throwing the error just below the mentioned line.

This is caused by the [polyfill](https://github.com/lifaon74/url-polyfill) not throwing when an invalid URL is created, like `new URL('/foo')`, and triggering a [different behavior](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/native-url/blob/66ed9808f9b995b80e66b7928817748a4da7afc7/src/parse.js#L99) on [`native-url`](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/native-url).
A PR has just been merged regarding this bug and will hopefully get published soon https://github.com/lifaon74/url-polyfill/pull/54

title: Garbage explosion (memory leak type issue)
body: # Bug report After update of NextJS node garbage collector (scavenger) in SSR service started to run very frequently up to consuming all CPU and basically making service non-responsive. ## Describe the bug While tracking down the issue we isolated that it is caused by some change in https://github.com/zeit/next.js/releases/tag/v9.0.6-canary.1 . I can't see any obvious culprit in there but all versions canary.0 and below are stable and canary.1 and later are not. It is happening also in latest stable version 9.3.4. The issue isn't classic memory leak where something would stay in memory for too long but it is that a lot of garbage is generated in new space and immediately collected. We concluded that because total memory usage is stable, increasing size of new space (`--max-semi-space-size`) increases time it takes exhaust the cpu, there are no major leftovers between heap snapshots and the CPU is consumed by `scavenger` (minor gc that runs only in new space) which frequency is increasing very rapidly. See the screenshot below. In profiler or memory debugger we haven't found any clear suspect the only thing that didn't seem right and were memory allocations within `require`, see attached screenshot. (Also head@reduceComponents but we ruled them out / fixed by replacing that with helmet) ## To Reproduce Unfortunately I wasn't able to reproduce it anywhere else then in production environment, but that is probably due to shape of traffic. ## Expected behavior Not crash the service ## Screenshots ## System information - OS: node 12.16.0 (tested also on v13), inside docker & kubernetes - Version of Next.js: >= 9.0.6-canary.1 - Memory limit is set to 1GB and `max-old-space-size` to 900MB ## Additional context Here are our .babelrc.js, next.config.js, tsconfig.json https://gist.github.com/jakubriedl/d5c306d5cf2862ea468387681eb3a53d Some main packages we combine next with - Apollo - StyledComponents - Custom server using express - Typescript Also all our pages are SSR and cached on CDN where possible, we don't use SSG at this moment.

# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I've been looking through the docs and I can't seem to find any information on how to redirect. There used to be a [wiki page](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/wiki/Redirecting-in-getInitialProps/) but that got deleted, and so the only information I could find are in GitHub issues.

1. So it seems okay to redirect in `getInitialProps`, however that is being deprecated in favor of `getServerSideProps`. Is it safe to redirect in there?
2. However, @Timer said that you shouldn't redirect in `getInitialProps` using the client-side router ([here](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/4931#issuecomment-512787861)). Which makes the method that was mentioned in the original wiki page incorrect.

So what is the best way to redirect in the current version of next? Looking at zeit.co it looks like its being done in `getInitialProps` but I can't be sure. If I had to venture a guess you should do it in `getServerSideProps` and `useEffect` in the function for client-side redirection.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A page that describes the recommended way to redirect on the server-side and/or client side.

N/A

# Bug report
NextJS simply ignores any OPTIONS request that has Origin in the header and won't execute the function.

## Describe the bug
After [Following the documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-routes/api-middlewares#connectexpress-middleware-support) and implementing the middleware to handle cors, it seems seems like it gets triggered *ONLY* when there's no Origin header in the OPTIONS request.

In other words, put a `console.log` at the beginning of the function (before cors middleware). Send an OPTIONS request without Origin in the headers, see the log. Now add Origin (any value) and the log doesn't even show up. The function was not executed.

## To Reproduce

1. Start with a fresh NextJS app
2. Follow [the documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-routes/api-middlewares#connectexpress-middleware-support)
3. Use Postman to send an OPTIONS request and see the cors middleware returning the right response
4. Add Origin in the headers (to simluate a browser) and watch as the api function doesn't get called.

## Expected behavior

NextJS should allow me to handle CORS requests.

title: Incorrect prefetch urls with BasePath
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Deployed a NextJS app under a basePath and any route change was causing a full page render, so no SPA behaviour. Looking into the network console and the js bundle is failing to fetch on route change. The request url isn't correct.

Here is how the request url is:
```
https://test.domain.com/ZONE/_next/static/k9DBUeMqYI7E5aV7S00Am/pages/ZONE/users.js
```

The basePath `ZONE` is being included in two different parts of the url and fails to fetch since this path doesn't exist on the app.

See also discussion about this issue: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/11912

## To Reproduce

Have a NextJS app deployed with a basePath and click on a Link.

## Expected behavior

I would expect this request url:
```
https://test.domain.com/ZONE/_next/static/k9DBUeMqYI7E5aV7S00Am/pages/users.js
```

Tested that url and it fetches the js successfully.

body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

I have assetPrefix set because we are hosting multiple applications on the same domain and use a proxy to route paths. 

`assetPrefix = "reports"`

The static asset urls are correct. Such as `/reports/_next/static/development/pages/_app.js?ts=1587171521639`.

However, the data fetching URLs are NOT including the prefix: `/_next/data/development/reports/appointments/2020-03-18/2020-04-17.json`.


## To Reproduce

- Set assetPrefix to anything
- Create a page with `getServerSideProps`
- use the router (or Link) to go to that page on the client
- Observe in the network request inspector that the data urls do not include the assetPrefix.

## Expected behavior

I would expect the assetPrefix to apply to ALL asset urls that start with `_next/`

title: Catch all route `foo/[...slug].tsx` also match path `foo`
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently catch all routes can be defined by a file like `foo/[...slug].tsx` and matches a path like `http://next.js/foo/bar`. We use nextjs in combination with react-router to support nested views. So our use case requires the path `http://next.js/foo` to be matched by `foo/[...slug].tsx`.

## Describe the solution you'd like
be able to setup the page via `foo/[...slug].tsx` and resolve uris like `http://next.js/foo`

## Describe alternatives you've considered
As workaround we setup `foo.tsx` to resolve `http://next.js/foo` and created a symbolic link of `foo.tsx` to `foo/[...slug].tsx`.

## Additional context
We decided to integrate react-router because our nested views are very dynamic and an implementation with nextjs only is too complex (maintaining this, too).

title: Add watch mode to the next build CLI
body:
# Feature request

Adding an optional watch mode `-w,--watch` to the `next build` CLI.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Also, describe any alternatives you've considered. 

Using cypress for e2e testing, while running `next dev`, can lead to tests timing out since it can sometimes take longer than 4 seconds before next (re)compiles the requested page. In addition, if you concurrently run `next dev` with `cypress open` or `cypress run`, the tests can fail when a route has to be (re)compiled -- in my case when a compilation event occurs, the tests fail because cypress triggers a `before` and `after` database seed/teardown in the middle of it). 

The alternative has been to run two separate processes while increasing the `defaultCommandTimeout` in the cypress global [Timeouts](https://docs.cypress.io/guides/references/configuration.html#Timeouts) config. Unfortunately, this has the added side effect of slower testing (as next needs to recompile on the fly) and allows your tests to run longer before they timeout/fail. This is worsened by the fact that some computers might have slower/older processors and require longer timeouts. 

The best solution I've found has been to compile the entire application using next build for a `staging` environment. This eliminates recompilations/webpack reloads on route changes, which allows the two processes to run concurrently, which results in faster testing times and doesn't require an increased global command timeout. However, the major downside has been that every time I need to make an adjustment to my application, I have to: stop the concurrent processes, manually recompile the entire application and then rerun the concurrent processes again -- which can take anywhere from 1-2 minutes per change (most of these changes I'm making are for testing purposely only; where I'm adding an additional `data-test` attribute for simpler tests because styled-components doesn't create static class names).

## Describe the solution you'd like

Similar to webpack's [watch](https://webpack.js.org/configuration/watch/) mode in **production**, this should improve the (re)building process times from 1-2mins per change down to 1-3s per change.

## Additional context

The [Next CLI documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/cli) needs to be updated with `options`. For example, it seems to be missing documentation on options like `-p` for a custom port.

title: Tsconfig path should be configurable
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Next will automatically use the root `tsconfig.json` as the config for its build.

Specifically problem is that it clashes with other project tooling:

- VS Code will use this config as the source of truth, so you can't exclude test files, Storybook stories etc. otherwise they won't be correctly typed in the text editor

- Next will use this config for its build, so you should exclude irrelevant files, in order to at least fasten the build even if the files will end up not being used.

## To Reproduce

Install TS in an app.
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "allowJs": false,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "baseUrl": "./",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "lib": [
      "dom",
      "dom.iterable",
      "esnext"
    ],
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "node",
    "noEmit": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "strict": false,
    "target": "es5",
    "paths": {
      "~/*": [
        "src/*"
      ]
    }
  },
  "exclude": [
    "node_modules",
    "**/*.stories.tsx",
    "**/stories.tsx"
  ],
  "include": [
    "next-env.d.ts",
    "**/*.ts",
    "**/*.tsx"
  ]
}
```
The `exclude` part is conflicting, I need it to optimize Next bundle, I must remove it for VS Code to work (and VS code does not allow to configure a different tsconfig path either).

Note that the `.storybook` folder has a `tsconfig.json` that includes stories, but it does not work, VS code still respect the root tsconfig `exclude`.

## Expected behavior

We should have a separate `tsconfig.next.json` file, either as a default or optionnaly, to avoid clashes with other tooling. Using the default `tsconfig.json` file is sadly a common practice but not realistic in a real life application.

Any other escape hatch to solve this would be welcome.

To sum it up `tsconfig.json` should be considered as a kind of `tsconfig.common.json`, that is shared by all config but optimized for none. So it should always be possible to specify it a bit more.

## System information

- Version of Next.js: 9.3


## Additional context
My app is setup with Jest, cypress, Storybook, Next custom server, and Next. Each environment needs a slightly different tsconfig with a shared common basis. Only Next client part do not allow configuration of the tsconfig file path.

title: Importing correctly scoped css from node_modules outside of _app
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Importing a stylesheet from a package is not possible in a page, because next throws with this error:

```
Global CSS cannot be imported from files other than your Custom <App>. Please move all global CSS imports to pages/_app.tsx.
Read more: https://err.sh/next.js/css-global
```

While I understand where this stems from, it makes code-splitting impossible. If I import a component from a component library, I need to import the CSS as well. There might be libraries that don't correctly scope their selectors, but that shouldn't stop me from overwriting this warning. CSS that is imported from a library isn't inherently "global".

## To Reproduce

1. `import "my-library/index.css"`
2. `yarn dev`
3. I get the error from above

## Expected behavior

The file should be imported.

I see these possible solutions:

* Global flag in `next.config.js`
* Comment annotation on import
* Warn instead of completely blocking it
* Check if the CSS only contains scoped selectors

## Additional context

There have been previous discussions about this.

### From the [blog](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-9-2#built-in-css-support-for-global-stylesheets)

> Since stylesheets are global by nature, they must be imported in the Custom <App> component. This is necessary to avoid class name and ordering conflicts for global styles.

I disagree with this statement, the reasoning being that an external library can use CSS modules and package them as a CSS file to import. Which is perfectly valid and common practice and *does not have side effects*.

### #10059

This issue got closed because the global import in `_app` is the correct choice there.
This [comment](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/10059#issuecomment-607444285)  describes the exact problem, but there hasn't been any response, as the issue is closed. The comment got a lot of positive reactions though, so I suppose I'm not the only one with this problem.

### #10975

Seems to be unrelated.

### #9830

Might be related, but I'm not sure.

## My use case

I write long articles with a lot of custom artwork and interactive illustrations. Articles use private npm packages with react components that render SVG with quite a bit of CSS. These packages use CSS modules and export an `index.js` and `index.css`. Adding all the CSS files to `_app` causes all the CSS to be loaded, even if people are on the home page, the contact form, or any other article, even though it's 100% unused. It also goes against having the file system take care of your pages because almost every page corresponds to a CSS import in `_app`.

title: Feature: Multiple path segments in page filenames
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I am a big fan of Next's file system router. However, with dynamic routes, it can lead to deeper folder structures than I would like.

For example, if I have CRUD routes for "bands" and "albums", where each "album" belongs to a "band", I end up with the following folder structure in `pages`:

```sh
# 1 folder deep
bands/index.js
bands/new.js
# 2 folders deep
bands/[bandId]/index.js
bands/[bandId]/edit.js
bands/[bandId]/delete.js
# 3 folders deep
bands/[bandId]/albums/index.js
bands/[bandId]/albums/new.js
# 4 folders deep
bands/[bandId]/albums/[albumId]/index.js
bands/[bandId]/albums/[albumId]/edit.js
bands/[bandId]/albums/[albumId]/delete.js
```

Personally, I find:

1. the deep folder structure gets unmanageable (especially when the hierarchy is deeper).
2. it's unnatural to have pages related to "bands" split between two folders `bands` and `bands/[bandId]`.

## Describe the solution you'd like

#### Possible solution 1

It would be easier to get a flat folder structure if multiple path segments could be included in a single filename. i.e. filenames like `[xxx]yyy.js` or `[xxx][yyy].js`.

The above example could become:

```sh
# 1 folder deep
bands/index.js
bands/new.js
bands/[bandId].js
bands/[bandId]edit.js
bands/[bandId]delete.js
# 2 folders deep
bands/[bandId]albums/index.js
bands/[bandId]albums/new.js
bands/[bandId]albums/[albumId].js
bands/[bandId]albums/[albumId]edit.js
bands/[bandId]albums/[albumId]delete.js
```

This has nested folders only 2-deep rather than 4, and the `[bandId]albums` folder contains all 5 files related to "albums" in one place.

I imagine this could be achieved as simply as using a regex on file paths before they are converted to routes `path.replace(/\](?!\.)/g, ']/')`.

#### Possible solution 2

Make some "special" character in filenames be treated as a slash. e.g. `~`.

```sh
# 1 folder deep
bands/index.js
bands/new.js
bands/[bandId].js
bands/[bandId]~edit.js
bands/[bandId]~delete.js
# 2 folders deep
bands/[bandId]~albums/index.js
bands/[bandId]~albums/new.js
bands/[bandId]~albums/[albumId].js
bands/[bandId]~albums/[albumId]~edit.js
bands/[bandId]~albums/[albumId]~delete.js
```

This doesn't produce any better result for my use case, but it's more flexible. Someone else might want to flatten a structure with routes which don't use dynamic paths e.g. `pages/some/deep/structure.js` -> `some~deep~structure.js`.

#### Possible solution 3

Either of the above would be (strictly speaking) be a breaking change. Someone somewhere might have a page called `[foo]bar.js` and want its url to be static at `http://mysite.com/[foo]bar` - which is what they'd get at present.

A way to introduce this functionality in a non-breaking way would be to add an option to `next.config.js` allowing the user to provide a custom file path -> URL path mapping function.

```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  transformFilePath(path) {
    return path.replace(/~/g, '/');
  }
};
```

This would also allow the user flexibility to do other kinds of path transformation/mapping.

I have a convention, for example, that params are always the same as the singular of the enclosing folder's name + `Id`. e.g. `bands/[bandId].js`, `albums/[albumId].js`. With a custom transform function, I could have terser file names e.g. `bands/[].js` and use the transform function to automatically flesh them out to `bands/[bandId].js`.

I imagine this would not be too difficult to implement for server and dev environments, but I'm not sure if it'd hugely complicate serverless deployment.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Perhaps using a custom server would allow this, but that would rule out SSG.

Maybe it's somehow possible through custom webpack config, but I'm not sure. If anyone thinks that is a viable solution I'd hugely appreciate any pointers.

I don't *think* this is covered by #9081.

## Additional context

If you'd be willing to accept one of the above solutions (or something else which fulfils my use case), I'd be happy to implement and submit a PR.

title: Add configuration option to disable API routing.
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm trying to use `/api` as a landing page that introduces users to the product's API and links them to the full documentation, but I can't find any way to disable Next's API routing - instead, it just tries to turn the page into an API endpoint.

https://nextjs.org/docs/api-routes/introduction

## Describe the solution you'd like

It'd be useful to have a configuration option to disable API routing for sites built on Next that are purely for marketing purposes.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

I couldn't find any relevant configuration options and all of the other issues I was able to find on Google and GitHub involved redirecting from `/api` to a different route. I'm most likely going to go with that option if no other solution presents itself (it's not ideal, but at least the user would get redirected to the right place), but it seems odd that this feature is enforced with no way to opt-out.

title: [typescript] Add the possibility to extend `NextApiRequest` with custom fields
body:
# Feature request

It's often the case, when we add a middleware for example, that we need to add extra informations in the `req` object. 

```typescript
const handler = async (req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) => {
  req.session.set('user', user)
}
```

This emit a TS error:
```
Property 'session' does not exist on type 'NextApiRequest'.
```

I would like a way to extend the type `NextApiRequest` with `session` here for example.

Express tackles this problem with [declaration merging](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/declaration-merging.html#merging-interfaces): [see here](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/839738b973f370fa4d7e1fdad1fcb7deb528adf9/types/express-serve-static-core/index.d.ts#L18-L26).

As a temporary workaround, I created a custom type, but that's not ideal because it forces me to import this type instead of the "builtin" type next provides.

```typescript
export type NextApiRequestWithSession = NextApiRequest & {
  session: Session
}

# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Currently it is not possible to activate a `<Link>` that wraps a by default non interactive component (like a `div` or a `tr`) by pressing the enter key. This is something that should be included by default imo. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/Keyboard-navigable_JavaScript_widgets says that any clickable object should be activatable using the keyboard. The reason it already works for `<a>` is because this element handles the keyboard events under the hood.

## To Reproduce

```jsx
<Link href="/abc">
   <tr role="button" tabIndex={0}>
      ...   
   </tr>
</Link>
```

1. Select the `<tr>` using tab
2. Press [enter]
3. Navigation does not occur

## Expected behavior

`next/link` should not just listen to `onClick` events but also `onKeyDown` with the key == "enter".

title: [BUG] Next's polyfills don't support @nivo packages in IE11
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Currently using [nivo](https://github.com/plouc/nivo) in a project for some simple charting. Specifically, I'm using the `@nivo/bar` and `@nivo/pie` packages, which happen to have some ES6 syntax (from their `d3-scale` dependency) that causes IE11 to crash. The workaround I used (before switching to next) was to utilize these options provided by `preset-env`:
```js
presets: [
   [ "@babel/preset-env", { useBuiltIns: "entry", corejs: { version: 3, proposals: true } } ],
]
```
In addition, I would include these 2 imports:
```js
import "core-js/stable"; 
import "regenerator-runtime/runtime"
```
into my application's main `index.js` file. 

With that, I was able to load the charts within [IE11 in a production environment](https://i.imgur.com/PNpYfnN.png).

Unfortunately, the polyfills provided by next don't seem to be enough for the nivo charts to be loaded properly in IE11. Instead, it quietly hangs when attempting to view a page with a chart. 

## To Reproduce

1.) Clone this repo: `git@github.com:mattcarlotta/nivo-IE11-example.git`
2.) Install deps: `yarn`
3.) Run `yarn dev`
4.) Start up a virtual sandbox to Windows 10 (or install repo locally on Windows 10)
5.) Load IE11 and visit `http://10.0.2.2:3001` or `http://localhost:3001` (if installed locally)
6.) Click on the `Bar` or `Chart` links -- the page won't navigate
7.) Click on the `Test` link -- page navigates to test

## Expected behavior

To navigate to a page and load the charts.

## Screenshots

Here are some screenshots to showcase that the `/bar` page works in...

Chrome (latest):
![](https://i.imgur.com/94flfJF.png)

FF (latest):
![](https://i.imgur.com/Q8reSb0.png)

Edge (latest, non-chromium):
![](https://i.imgur.com/8c70dGn.png)

Meanwhile... IE11 (latest)
Home page loads (clicking on the `Bar` or `Pie` links does nothing)
![](https://i.imgur.com/iNzs6jO.png)
However, clicking on the `Test` page loads as expected
![](https://i.imgur.com/FaN2xM5.png)


## System information

- OS: LMDE 4
- Version of Next.js: v9.3.5
- Version of Node.js: v10.20.1

## Additional context

Is there a way to target the `d3-scale` package and transpile to ES5 (which appears to require babel's runtime regenerator) or perhaps include a polyfill?

body:
Hello there!

# Bug report

Built-In CSS-Support failing for valid CSS.

## Describe the bug

When attempting to import a CSS file using the built-in css-imports fails. 
I was able to pinpoint the exact rule that causes the complication, see below.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Clone this repository: https://github.com/MrAvantiC/next-css-import-issue
2. Run `npm install && npm run dev`
3. You will notice that the build process will fail with the following line:
```sh
[ error ] ./public/main.css (./node_modules/css-loader/dist/cjs.js??ref--5-oneOf-5-1!./node_modules/next/dist/compiled/postcss-loader??__nextjs_postcss!./public/main.css)
CssSyntax error: Unclosed bracket (2:2)

  1 | .foo {
> 2 |   flex: 1 0 calc(30% - (30px / 3));
    |  ^
  3 | }
  4 |
```

The CSS itself is completely valid, which i confirmed with several linterns.

The error seems to be caused by the inner bracket inside the `calc` operator because as soon as you rewrite it, e.g. `flex: 1 0 calc(30% - 30px);` everything is working fine.

**Side note**

I tested the exact same setup using the [next-css package](https://github.com/zeit/next-plugins/tree/master/packages/next-css) and *it works completely fine*.
You can find the example in the [with-next-css branch of the same repository](https://github.com/MrAvantiC/next-css-import-issue/tree/with-next-css).

So there seems to be a difference between both mechanisms.

## Expected behavior

The server should compile without problems as it does using the next-css package, see above.

## System information

- OS: macOs
- Version of Next.js:9.3.5
- Version of Node.js: 13.9.0

title: Build error when slug ends with `.html` for dynamic routes
body:
# Bug report

I have an old site which I'm about to migrate to Next.js. I want to generate static pages. I have to support URLs such as: `/blog/article-slug.html` (this is the canonical URL that users and search engines see). I found two ways to build such URLs but neither of them seem to work properly.

## Describe the bug

### Option 1
I create a page component such as `pages/blog/[slug].html.js` and in `getStaticPaths` I provide the `slug` without the `.html` extension.

```js
export const getStaticPaths = async () => {
    return { fallback: false, paths: [{ params: { slug: 'article-slug' } }] };
};
```
This options does not work at all. I DEV mode I only get a 404 page if I try to access `http://localhost:3000/blog/article-slug.html`. When running `next build` I get
> Error: getStaticPaths can only be used with dynamic pages, not '/articles/[slug].html'.
This means that this page is considered to have a static path and not be a dynamic.

### Option 2

I create a page component such as `pages/blog/[slug].js` and in `getStaticPaths` I provide the `slug` with the `.html` extension.

```js
export const getStaticPaths = async () => {
    return { fallback: false, paths: [{ params: { slug: 'article-slug.html' } }] };
};
```

This option at least works in DEV mode. But when running `next build` I get the following error:
```
> Build error occurred
[Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename '/tmp/next/.next/export/blog/article-slug.html.html' -> '/tmp/next/.next/server/static/78zmPfx5_aE06CmpsBKfD/pages/blog/article-slug.html.html'] {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ENOENT',
  syscall: 'rename',
  path: '/tmp/next/.next/export/blog/article-slug.html.html',
  dest: '/tmp/next/.next/server/static/78zmPfx5_aE06CmpsBKfD/pages/blog/article-slug.html.html'
}
```

## To Reproduce

I created a repo to reproduce these errors:  
https://github.com/bdadam/next.js-error-when-.html-in-path

## Expected behavior

I would expect that `next build` generates a file such as `.next/export/blog/article-slug.html.html`.

## System information

- OS: Linux, Ubuntu 19.10
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.5
- Version of Node.js: 13.6.0

## Other considerations

I can only reproduce this behavior if the slug ends with `.html` a `.` itself in the slug does not seem to cause any problems e.g. `article....slug.xhtml`.

body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Not a problem but an potential performance improvement. For example a blog website:
- page `blog/[slug]` will use `getStaticProps` if the post is **published** and `getServerSideProps` if the post is still in draft.

So most of the posts will use **Static Generation** with all the benefits.

Only the draft ones will be generated on each request since they are subject to be changed often.

This can also be applied for `E-Commerce Product pages`, `Documentation`, `Marketing pages`,...

## Describe the solution you'd like
One solution would be allowing `getServerSideProps` and `getStaticProps` in the same page, if `getStaticProps` return `null`, use `getServerSideProps`.

No

title: Ignore GSSP on next export
body:
# Feature request

I expected `next export` to exclude any pages featuring GSSP. The desire is to use next's built-in method to hoist all static content to a particular folder.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I am re-working the Firebase examples and want to leverage the Firebase CDN in a better way. [Firebase Hosting priority order](https://firebase.google.com/docs/hosting/full-config#hosting_priority_order) can be used to have all static resources on Firebase Hosting served first by the CDN and any request misses be fulfilled by the Cloud Functions hosted Next.js app. This requires me to run `next export` (I want to avoid duplicating this functionality myself) to produce the static resources to push to the CDN.

However, with SSG, the page is computed by the backend a single time if missing. I desire some pages to be SSR with GSSP.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I would like a flag for `next export` to override the existing behavior which errors with:

```
Error occurred prerendering page "/index". Read more: https://err.sh/next.js/prerender-error:
Error: Error for page /index: pages with `getServerSideProps` can not be exported. See more info here: https://err.sh/next.js/gssp-export
```

For example: `next export --ignore-gssp` which performs as it does today, but **skips pages with GSSP**.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Using SSG mode with an empty paths `paths:[], fallback:true` works with `next export` and forces all content to be computed on request (doesn't generate any build time `.html` or `.json`), but only once. This method also only works for dynamic routes `/posts/[id].js`. Not quite the behavior I want.

Using SSG mode with a per-page CDN cache flush is also a possibility, though highly dependent on the Hosting service. Firebase for instance, does not have any CDN cache flush or cache control outside of `s-maxage`. CDN cache flushing would also require tracking of BUILD_ID as it is used in the path for the `.json` data. 

Using SSR mode with a large `s-maxage` & CDN cache flush is also possible, again, dependent on Hosting service and it's availability of cache flushing.

I have considered:

1. creating my own copy command to perform the hoist of static resources. From the source I can see:

	```
	1. (copy static folder)
	.next/static                         -> out/_next/static
	
	2. (copy SSG .html files (without route regex in name))
	.next/server/static/{build_id}/pages -> out/
	
	3. (copy SSG .json data files)
	.next/server/static/{build_id}/pages -> out/_next/data/{build_id}
	
	4. (copy public folder)
	public                               -> out/
	```
	
	This way I wouldn't need to use `next export`, dynamic-route SSG pages would be computed on first request and SSR pages on each request :thinking: 

## Additional context

- `next 9.3.5`

---

For those finding this, I have created an example script: https://gist.github.com/jthegedus/8e820d37e1f3768f991886fb65de154f

title: Styles duplicated across css chunks create source order issues
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug
I have an application that uses a component on multiple pages. When I build the project that component's styles are duplicated in each of the relevant css page chunks; this creates visual bugs.

For example (`some-component`, and `initial-page-component-override` are classes applied to the same element in the DOM on the initial page):

**initial-page.chunk.css**
```
// component styles
.some-component { margin-bottom: 10px; }

// page specific override
.initial-page-component-override { margin-bottom: 20px; }
```

**second-page.chunk.css**
```
// component styles
.some-component { margin-bottom: 10px; }
```

When second-page.chunk.css is added to the DOM the component styles are reapplied over the top of any page specific styles defined in the initial page. The overrides are lost and the incorrect margin is now applied to the component on the initial page. N.B. this is not an issue in dev mode, only in production.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Checkout https://github.com/petewarman/nextjs-css-module-issue
2. `npm i`, `npm run build`, `npm start`
3. Hover the cursor over the lime green button 
4. See it change to pink when the second page's stylesheet is preloaded

## Expected behavior

Style declarations should not be duplicated in compiled stylesheets. Component styles should loaded (in their own chunk?) above page specific styles.

## System information

- OS: macOS
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.6
- Version of Node.js: 10.16.3

title: [Feature Request] native static sitemaps
body:
# Feature request
Provide a static sitemap feature out of the box.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
For some listings(e.g. google for jobs) sitemaps are essential or at least a boost.
In pre next 9 a lot of users resorted to using an api route or custom server to generate the sitemap on the fly.

## Describe the solution you'd like
For pages utilizing SSG the sitemap could be generated alongside/or in a post build (it more or less already is in the console output) step. Not sure if that makes sense for mixed (lambda + ssg) sites, but for full-static i imagine this could be relatively low effort high impact feature.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
One could implement this in userland, by just iterating trough the build output folder as an externalized post build step.

## Additional context
*Not trying to start a flame war on pricing here, but i guess it belongs into context :sweat_smile:!*
In recent history vercel/now pricing/api limits were altered limiting the amount of lambdas one project is allowed to have(12) pushing a lot of users into the server side generation.
I'm currently migrating some hobby projects to SSG and am trying to drop as many function calls as possible, but while 12 sounds like a lot you'll quickly max them out when providing endpoints for push notifications/email-subscription/sitemap/...
Sitemaps seem like an easy thing to do less dynamically especially with the beauty of SSG and periodic/triggered invalidation.

When testing with Jest and rendering a `<Link>` component, clicking the link fails with `No router instance found.` error because we are running outside of the browser.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

[Here is a codesandbox](https://codesandbox.io/s/recursing-lehmann-blvlq?file=/__tests__/testint-library.js) based on the `with-jest` example.

If you comment out `fireEvent.click` on the link, the tests will pass. The problem is, we should be able to click links in testing and make sure that something happened. For example, I want to test that my `<NavButton>` component, which is backed by a `Link`, actually routes the user properly.  

## Expected behavior

The test should pass, ideally navigating jsdom appropriately. 

When testing, we often need/want to closely replicate the browser environment. If we must mock the linking and routing behavior, it would be useful if Next provided a way to implement or mock the Router and Link contexts. For reference, when using react-router, after clicking the link, I can access the `history.location.pathname` and see that it has changed appropriately. 

I suppose it is possible to mock out all of `next/link`, but my personal philosophy is to avoid mocks unless absolutely necessary since production bugs often occur at integration points.

I also feel that this testing links should be made part of the `with-jest` example. 

## Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4398775/80778485-cd249900-8b25-11ea-94b2-2200ae116feb.png)


## Attempted solutions

I have searched the issues and attempted a few mentioned solutions, including:
1. mocking `useRouter` with a mock router object
2. providing mock `RouterContext` by importing the internal `RouterContext.Provider` component and wrapping my test in that. 

Neither of these work because it appears next is internally using a singleton router instance, which is unavailable in jsdom.

## My suggestion

I would suggest adding a `<NextTestContext>` component which provides the test context and environment necessary (such as the browser-only functionality) for testing. Allows passing in mock values for things like router. Not sure if this is possible or what you'd want, but if you point me in the right direction, I'm happy to submit a PR.

Alternatively, if this should be solved another way, I am happy to make a docs PR too. Just let me know. It seems there are many conflicting recs in the issues, it might be useful to have testing docs.

title: Using getServerSideProps breaks scroll restoration
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

When using getServerSideProps, a server roundtrip is made every time the user navigates to a page, to load the page's data json (generated by getServerSideProps).

This _also_ happens when the page is navigated to _via the browser's back and forward buttons_. The latency of the request, even when cached, breaks browser-native scroll restoration.

As there is no way to intervene with the request on the client side (using getServerSideProps, the request is made Next-internally), it can't be blocked. Using getInitialProps, it was possible to cache data on the client side and return it immediately. This is not possible anymore with getServerSideProps.

## To Reproduce

The issue is sufficiently documented [here](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/3303).

## Expected behavior

Pages using getServerSideProps do not break scroll restoration when navigated to via the browser's back/forward buttons.

title: Webpack's resolve.mainFields and resolve.alias doesn't work as expected in the server environment
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

`resolve.mainFields` and `resolve.alias` doesn't affect files in `node_modules`:

```js
const path = require("path");

module.exports = {
  webpack: (config, { isServer }) => {
    if (isServer) config.resolve.mainFields.splice(0, 0, "ssr");

    config.resolve.alias["alias-local/message$"] = path.resolve(
      __dirname,
      "alias.js"
    );

    config.resolve.alias["alias-modules/message$"] = path.resolve(
      __dirname,
      "alias.js"
    );

    return config;
  },
};
```

The configuration works when I load a local module, but fails when a load it from `node_modules`.

## To Reproduce

1. Clone [the repo](https://github.com/kossnocorp/next-webpack-config-bug) `git clone https://github.com/kossnocorp/next-webpack-config-bug.git`
2. `cd next-webpack-config-bug`
3. `yarn`
4. `cp -r alias-modules node_modules`
5. `cp -r main-fields node_modules`
6. `yarn dev`

To see the main fields error:

1. Open http://localhost:3000/main-fields-local and [view-source:http://localhost:3000/main-fields-local](view-source:http://localhost:3000/main-fields-local)
2. See that it renders "Main fields works as expected (browser)!" and "Main fields works as expected (SSR)!" respectively
3. Open http://localhost:3000/main-fields-modules
4. See the error

The see the alias error:

1. Open http://localhost:3000/alias-local
2. See that it renders "Alias works as expected!"
3. Open http://localhost:3000/alias-modules
4. See the error

## Expected behavior

The `resolve.mainFields` and `resolve.alias` should work for modules in `node_modules` the same way it works for the local ones.

## System information

- OS: macOS
- Version of Next.js: 9.3.6
- Version of Node.js: 10.16.3

## Additional context

I [maintain a library](https://github.com/kossnocorp/typesaurus) that allows using Firestore both in the browser and Node.js. I achieve that providing a special "submodule" that has `package.json` with the given context:

```json
{
  "browser": "./browser/index",
  "main": "./node"
}
```

A user is [struggling to use Typesaurus with Next.js](https://github.com/kossnocorp/typesaurus/issues/49) because Next.js in the server environment is trying to load `firebase-admin`, which supposed to be used only for Node.js. That is a problem on my side, but I can't provide a fix because of the described issue.

I tried unsuccessfully to use alias or custom main fields property that would direct webpack to the correct file.

title: Object.keys non-object coercion not working in IE 11
body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

The argument passed to the `Object.keys` method should be coerced to an object from ES2015 onward. 
As illustrated in the example taken from https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/keys.
```
// In ES5
Object.keys('foo');  // TypeError: "foo" is not an object 

// In ES2015+
Object.keys('foo');  // ["0", "1", "2"]     
```

However, this behaviour is not pollyfilled in Next.js for IE 11.

## To Reproduce

1. Download the reproduction available at https://github.com/tomdohnal/object-keys-ie-repro
2. Use `yarn dev` or `npm run dev` to start the development server
3. Open the page in IE 11 and it crashes.

## Expected behavior

It should coerce the argument passed to Object.keys to object and not crash.

title: Add support for custom environments (Next 9.4)
body:
# Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, built-in environments allows only `.env.development` and `.env.production` environments, so when you run `yarn dev` it uses `.env.development` or `.env.local` and when you do `yarn build`, then `yarn start` it uses `.env.production` environment. But there's no way to use a staging environment for example, like `.env.staging`, there's no way to run app with staging environment, if we try to `NODE_ENV=staging yarn build && yarn start` we get an error: "https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/master/errors/non-standard-node-env.md", and it won't have effect, because `NODE_ENV` would be production anyway, it's being overwritten.

## Describe the solution you'd like

There should be a way to set environment when you run your app, like `NODE_ENV=staging/prestaging yarn build && yarn start`, etc. In CRA i use it this way:

```
"build:staging": "env-cmd -f .env.staging yarn build",
"build:prestaging": "env-cmd -f .env.prestaging yarn build"
```

Would be nice to have the same, but built-in in Next.

**PS**

`"build:staging": "env-cmd -f .env.staging yarn build && yarn start"` this actually works with Next either, though `NODE_ENV` would be set to "production".

title: Could you reconsider the "tsconfig.json" default value of "strict: false"?
body:
# Feature request

I just noticed that next.js defaults to `strict: false` in the generated `tsconfig.json`.

The reasoning behind seems to be (quoting @Timer from ##7716):

> Users who are testing out Next.js' TypeScript support shouldn't be stuck behind a failure to compile screen. This will allow advanced users to opt into strict: true when they're ready.

I would ask you if it were possible to reconsider this.

Running `tsc --init` creates a `tsconfig.json` with `strict: true` since that option was introduced with TypeScript 2.3. 
An advanced user will probably not notice this for quite some time, because they assume that TypeScript offers it's full (default-configuration) functionality out of the box, just wondering about unsound behaviour here and there until it piles up and finally going to `strict: true` has actually become a chore.

If there are any strict options that are not working well with next.js, it's still an option, to default to `strict: true` in combination with `strictThatHurts: false` and mentioning to that in the documentation.

I have to admit that I'm not even a next.js user myself (athough it is in my list of stuff to check out!), but got a report by a user of our library (@reduxjs/toolkit) about strange behaviour - which we could attribute back to `strictNullChecks` being disabled. The user was quite irritated because they had assumed that `strict` would be enabled.

So I don't really believe that you're doing your users a service with this default :(

As an alternative, if you could not commit to a `strict: true` default, maybe it might be an option to actively ask the user for feedback on it when the `tsconfig.json` would be filled with the default values - and let the user decide between "loose" and "strict" behaviour?

title: Allow Global CSS in Component Modules
body:
# Feature request
Hi I would like a setting to allow importing Global CSS in component Module.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I use many external components, some which require importing their CSS directly. The current rule of not allowing Global CSS in components has a few drawbacks for me:

1) We have to require all of these global css in _app which is a bad separation of concerns
2) Components that were lazy loaded dynamically will no longer have their CSS also loaded dynamically (page load bundle size is bigger which sucks because CSS is on the critical path to avoid FOUCs.
3) Its a lot harder to incrementally update, we have hundreds of components using global css format right now. Would like a way to adopt CSS Modules incrementally
4)  I'm aware of the issues talked about here: https://err.sh/next.js/css-global At Facebook the approach we took is to explicitly not depend on CSS ordering. Every build would randomly permute CSS to make such side effects obvious and more easily detectable. What we are doing now is forcing an explicit dependency on ordering, that means there will always be a danger when moving CSS across files. Instead people should be educated about relying on CSS Specificity instead which is the real solution to these issues.

A clear and concise description of what you want and what your use case is.
Allow referencing Global CSS in modules

## Describe alternatives you've considered

A build step that creates _app.tsx to avoid the issue of bad separation of concerns. 

## Additional context

For what its worth we should never be relying on CSS Ordering. We should be relying on CSS Specificity

title: Allow having an _app-like file for subpages
body:
# Feature request

First of all, thanks for building an awesome framework! :) 

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I have a use-case for which it would be nice to share layout (and persist state) across multiple subpages. Similar to what the [`_app`](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/custom-app) file allows for the entire application. In my specific case, I have a stateful sidebar component that I want to display on multiple subpages.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I was wondering if you've thought about supporting an `_app`-like file for subpages (e.g. named `_page`). I haven't considered any technical limitations or challenges that this might entail. But I was thinking about a folder structure like this:

- `some-page-folder`
  - `_page.tsx` (similar to `_app.tsx`)
  - `subpage.tsx` (automatically "wrapped" in `_page.tsx`)

## Describe alternatives you've considered

I've considered ditching next pages for this specific case, but I just like the simplicity of leveraging folder structure for pages. I've also considered modifying the `_app` file to accommodate my use-case, but that seems like a workaround to me.

Currently, I've added a `_page` in my own project which I then manually import for each subpage. It solves sharing the component. But it doesn't solve persisting state.

# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Environment variables are loaded in the following order:
```
ready - started server on http://localhost:3000
info  - Loaded env from .env.development.local
info  - Loaded env from .env.development
info  - Loaded env from .env.local
info  - Loaded env from .env
```
However, vars in `.env.local` do not overwrite vars in `.env.development`. Is this to be expected?

The use case arises when a var in development should be overwritten when running locally. Say accessing the api.

```
// .env.development
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="https://api.example.com"
```
```
// .env.local
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="http://localhost:3000"
